name: Brest
title: Brest Drydock Thickness Measurement | Ship UTM Gauging
description: Thickness measurement in Brest for ships in dry dock: renewal survey UTM, CAP gauging on tankers and LNG carriers, hull structure and pre-docking readings.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement in Brest's Dry Docks
intro: Brest is a repair port first. The three dry docks of Damen Shiprepair Brest, at the western tip of Brittany close to the Ushant traffic lanes, take LNG carriers, tankers, cruise ships, ferries and bulk carriers that come off their route between the Channel and the Atlantic to dock. Superintendents call us to gauge hull structure and tanks during those dockings, to support CAP on older tankers and to measure ahead of the yard stay. Our team travels from India for each docking, planned against the yard's date.

highlights.h: Large dry docks near the Ushant route
highlights.p: Damen Shiprepair Brest's dry docks take large LNG carriers, tankers and cruise ships close to the Ushant traffic lanes, so ships trading past Brittany can divert for docking with little deviation from their route.
Membrane LNG carriers are gauged from the ballast side, tankers through cargo and ballast tanks under the ESP Code. Brest's long, planned dockings suit both of these heavier scopes.
From September 2028 the Breton coast falls inside the North-East Atlantic ECA and its 0.10% sulphur limit. A docking here before then is the time to gauge scrubber wash-water and overboard piping.

port.h: Brest: a repair port on the approaches to the Channel
p: Brest sits on the Rade de Brest, a large and sheltered natural harbour at the western end of Brittany. Commercially it is a modest cargo port, handling agricultural bulk and general cargo for the region, and much of the roadstead belongs to the French Navy, whose Atlantic base is here. What brings deep-sea merchant ships to Brest is ship repair. The commercial port's dry docks, operated by Damen Shiprepair Brest, are large enough to take the biggest LNG carriers, crude tankers and cruise ships, and they are the reason a VLCC or a membrane LNG carrier is seen in a Breton harbour at all.

Location is the yard's commercial argument. Brest lies close to the Ushant traffic separation scheme, through which traffic between the Channel and the Atlantic passes, so a ship trading between northern Europe and the Atlantic, the Mediterranean or West Africa can come off its route for a docking with relatively little deviation. The yard's own list of the ships it docks runs from LNG carriers, crude, product and shuttle tankers to cruise ships, ferries, bulk carriers, container ships and offshore rigs, and it has carried out a long series of cruise ship refits. The combination of LNG carriers and older tankers is what gives Brest its particular gauging profile.

Because the work is docking-led, the gauging windows are long and planned: a ship arrives at the repair quay or the roadstead, enters dock on a booked date, and stays for the length of the repair specification. That makes Brest suited to the heavier scopes, such as renewal-survey gauging on tankers at their third or fourth renewal, CAP gauging that needs cargo tanks gas-free and staged, and LNG carrier dockings where ballast tanks, the inner hull and deck structure are measured from the ballast side. Ships waiting in the Rade or at the repair quay for their dock slot also give time for pre-docking readings, so that the steel list is fixed before the dock is flooded down.

facilities.h: Where gauging takes place in Brest
p: The three dry docks of Damen Shiprepair Brest are in the commercial port, with repair quays alongside for work afloat before and after docking. Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Brest is mostly done in these docks: the ship is dry, tanks are cleaned and ventilated for the repair contractors, and staging or access equipment is already in place for the yard's steelwork. The gauging team works to the yard's sequence, measuring tanks as soon as they are released and reporting by compartment so that renewal decisions are made early in the stay rather than in its last days.

The repair quays and the Rade anchorage are the other locations. A tanker or LNG carrier waiting for its dock slot can be gauged in its ballast tanks and on deck while alongside the repair quay or at anchor, so the steel list is known before the ship enters the dock. Weather counts in Brest: Atlantic depressions coming in past Ushant can halt launch work in the roadstead, and the yard's programme, not the team's travel plan, sets the date the work starts.
list: Damen Shiprepair Brest dry docks — docking and renewal-survey gauging of shell, tanks and internal structure on LNG carriers, tankers, cruise ships and bulk carriers.
Repair quays of the commercial port — pre-docking and post-docking gauging afloat, including ballast tanks and deck structure, while the ship waits for or leaves the dock.
Rade de Brest anchorage — launch-served readings on ships waiting for a dock slot, subject to Atlantic weather in the roadstead.
LNG carriers in dock — gauging of ballast tanks, the inner hull from the ballast side, cofferdams and deck structure during the docking.
Cruise ships and ferries in dock — gauging of shell plating, tanks and vehicle or open decks alongside the yard's refit and steel programme.

context.h: ECA boundary, port state control and Brest's place on the route
p: Brest is a useful reminder that the North Sea ECA has a western edge. Its limit in the Channel approaches runs along 5°W and 48°30'N, and Brest lies just south of that line, so a ship arriving from the Channel leaves the 0.10% sulphur area near Ushant. That changes in 2028. IMO adopted the North-East Atlantic ECA at MEPC 84 in 2026, covering the waters off France's Atlantic coast among others, with entry into force on 1 September 2027 and the 0.10% sulphur limit applying twelve months later. For scrubber-fitted ships docking at Brest, the coming ECA is a reason to have wash-water and overboard piping gauged while the ship is dry.

France is a Paris MoU state, and a ship leaving a Brest docking with its steel renewed and its readings on file is in a stronger position at its next port state control inspection. For tankers, a Brest docking often coincides with a renewal survey under the ESP Code: IACS UR Z10.4 for double-hull oil tankers and Z10.3 for chemical tankers set out the gauging and close-up survey, which grow sharply from the third renewal survey at about 15 years. Older tankers facing vetting can add CAP gauging to the same stay; once a tanker is past about 15 years, charterers and oil-major vetting departments frequently expect it. LNG carriers are not ESP ships; their hull gauging follows UR Z7 and the classification society's rules for gas carriers.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Brest
jobs.p: Almost every Brest job is tied to a dock booking, so the scope is known well ahead and the main variables are the yard date and the condition found. We work from the repair specification, the class's survey requirements and any previous gauging report, and size the team so readings keep pace with the yard. list: Fourth renewal survey gauging on a double-hull crude tanker in dock, covering cargo and ballast tank structure under the ESP Code, with close-up survey support for the attending surveyor.
CAP gauging in Brest on a product tanker over 15 years old, combined with its docking so cargo tanks are gas-freed and staged only once.
LNG carrier drydock gauging: ballast tanks, cofferdams and the inner hull of a membrane ship during its intermediate docking, all measured from the ballast side.
Pre-docking gauging at the repair quay on a bulk carrier, so the steel renewal estimate for holds and hopper tanks is ready on the day it enters dock.
Shell, tank and open-deck gauging on an expedition cruise ship during a refit, alongside the yard's steel and hotel work.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping gauging while a ship is in dock, ahead of the North-East Atlantic ECA sulphur limit in 2028.

logistics: Brest Bretagne Airport has connections from Paris, so the usual route is an international flight to Paris Charles de Gaulle followed by a domestic flight or a high-speed train to Brest. The yard and the ship's agent arrange access to the commercial port and the dry docks; the naval areas of the Rade are closed to civilians and play no part in the job. France is a Schengen state, so each technician needs a Schengen visa before travel, and we apply once the dock date is confirmed, with an invitation letter from the owner or yard naming the ship. If the dock date moves, the team's travel moves with it.

faqs.q: Is Brest inside the SOx ECA?
faqs.a: Not at present. The North Sea ECA's boundary in the Channel approaches runs along 5°W and 48°30'N, and Brest lies just south of it. The North-East Atlantic ECA adopted at MEPC 84 in 2026 will bring the Breton coast inside an ECA: it enters into force on 1 September 2027, with the 0.10% sulphur limit applying from September 2028.

faqs.q: Can you gauge an LNG carrier's inner hull during a Brest docking?
faqs.a: Yes, from the ballast side. On membrane LNG carriers the cargo tanks are lined, so the inner hull is measured from the ballast tanks and cofferdams, together with the outer shell, double bottom and deck structure. We plan the sequence with the yard so that ballast tanks are gauged as soon as they are ventilated and certified safe for entry, and report by tank so repairs can be decided in dock.

faqs.q: Can gauging start before the ship enters dock?
faqs.a: Often it should. A ship waiting at the repair quay or in the Rade for its dock slot can have ballast tanks and deck structure gauged in advance. Those readings let the superintendent confirm the steel list with the yard before docking, so the dock days are spent on repairs rather than on finding out what needs renewing.

faqs.q: What happens if the dock date at Brest slips?
faqs.a: Dock dates move, and the plan allows for it. Once the Schengen visas are issued, the team's flights are booked against the yard's latest confirmed date and changed if it moves. Telling us early about a slip, or about extra scope the yard has found, matters more than a perfect initial schedule, because it lets us adjust the team size as well as the dates.
